ei.subject: 공통영어1
ei.title: The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

fullPassage:
The Magic of Believing That You Can Grow

Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more. He rushes to the other side of the net and challenges his dad to a match.

Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.

The Boy Who Chooses an Easy and Familiar Path

Let's start with the path of avoidance. The boy waits for his dad and concentrates hard. When the ball comes flying across the net rapidly, he misses it completely. He puts his hands on his knees and sighs. "Never mind," says his dad, "Try again. Practice makes perfect."

When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room.

His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.

"No, thanks," sighs the boy. "He's going to be better than me anyway."

In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.

The Boy Who Embraces the Challenge

Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway.

An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a decent return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past his dad. The boy later on decides to challenge his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even harder.

The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent to be skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He realizes how far he has come. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of improving his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph. He has become truly awesome!

You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are ①<u>waiting</u> outside and pointing at the garage. When his dad pulls the garage door open, there ②<u>is</u> a table-tennis table inside! He rushes to the other side of the net and ③<u>challenges</u> his dad to a match. He recently ④<u>joining</u> the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ joining → joined. 과거 시제 문맥에서 동사 자리에 현재분사(joining)는 불가. 'recently joined'가 올바른 형태.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ④ joining: 주어 He + 동사 자리. 과거시제 joined 필요. joining(현재분사)은 동사 역할 불가.
❌ ① waiting: are waiting — 현재진행형. 올바름.
❌ ② is: there is + 단수명사(a table-tennis table). 올바름.
❌ ③ challenges: 3인칭 단수 현재. 올바름.
det.tip: 동사 자리에 -ing형만 단독으로 올 수 없다. be동사 없이 joining은 불가. He joined (O) / He joining (X).

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like ①<u>taking</u> up the challenge. When his mom suggests ②<u>playing</u> against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief ③<u>which</u> they are best ④<u>avoided</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ which → that. belief(추상명사) 뒤 동격절은 접속사 that으로 연결. 관계대명사 which는 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ which: the belief that they are best avoided — 동격의 that절. which 불가.
❌ ① taking: feel like + V-ing(~하고 싶다). 올바름.
❌ ② playing: suggest + V-ing. 올바름.
❌ ④ avoided: be avoided — 수동태. 올바름.
det.tip: 추상명사(belief, fact, idea, news) + that절 = 동격절. that은 접속사이므로 which로 대체 불가.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds his opponent ①<u>to be</u> skillful and smart, but he plays hard. He realizes how far he ②<u>has come</u>. For years he has gotten up early to practice and has loved the challenge of ③<u>improve</u> his game. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air ④<u>in</u> triumph.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ improve → improving. 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 와야 한다. 'the challenge of improving'이 올바른 형태.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ improve: 전치사 of + 동명사(improving) 필수. 동사원형 improve 불가.
❌ ① to be: find + O + to be + C(5형식). 올바름.
❌ ② has come: 현재완료. how far he has come(얼마나 멀리 왔는지). 올바름.
❌ ④ in: punch the air in triumph — 전치사 in. 올바름.
det.tip: 전치사(of, about, for 등) 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)만 가능. the challenge of improving (O) / the challenge of improve (X).

questions.passage: Let's rewind to the point when the boy first faces his dad across the net. His first attempt does not go any better, and he still gets hit on the elbow on his second try. However, he picks up the ball and tries again anyway. An hour later, his dad still keeps winning easily, but the boy is learning from the experience. The boy later on decides to ①<u>avoid</u> his older brother. His brother is a better player, but the boy likes the idea that he can work even ②<u>harder</u>. Every now and then, he even surprises himself with a ③<u>decent</u> return, and a few times, he almost hits the ball past ④<u>his dad</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① avoid → challenge. 원문: 'decides to challenge his older brother.' 도전을 받아들이는 맥락에서 avoid(피하다)는 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ① avoid: 원문은 challenge(도전하다). 형을 피하는 것이 아니라 도전하는 맥락.
❌ ② harder: 원문 그대로.
❌ ③ decent: 원문 그대로(괜찮은).
❌ ④ his dad: 원문 그대로.
det.tip: challenge(도전하다) ↔ avoid(피하다). 도전을 받아들이는 소년의 태도와 일치하는 단어 선택.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his ①<u>passion</u> for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly ②<u>desired</u>, and then became ③<u>fragile</u> when he faced a difficult task. You, too, can find your own "table tennis." What is important is that you ④<u>embrace</u> the challenge and never give up.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중, 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ fragile → tough. 원문: 'became tough when he faced a difficult task.' 어려운 과제에 직면했을 때 강해졌다는 맥락에서 fragile(약한)은 부적절.
det.analysis:
✅ 정답 ③ fragile: 원문은 tough(강인한). 성장 마인드셋으로 어려움에 강해졌다는 맥락에 fragile(취약한) 부적절.
❌ ① passion: 원문 그대로(열정).
❌ ② desired: 원문 그대로(원했다).
❌ ④ embrace: 원문 그대로(받아들이다).
det.tip: tough(강인한) ↔ fragile(취약한). growth mindset = 어려움에 강해지는 태도.

questions.passage: Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to __________ and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.
questions.stem: 위 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: give up on his dreams entirely
ask his parents for more help
find a different sport to play

det.korean: 소년은 스스로에게 도전하여 성장하고 어려움에 맞서거나, 쉽고 익숙한 길을 택하는 선택의 기로에 서 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① challenge himself to grow: 원문 직접 인용. '스스로에게 도전하여 성장하다'.
❌ ② give up: 포기가 아닌 회피(avoid)가 원문의 반대 선택.
❌ ③ ask parents: 부모에게 도움 요청 언급 없음.
❌ ④ different sport: 다른 스포츠 언급 없음.
det.tip: challenge himself to grow ↔ avoid and choose an easy path. 원문의 대비 구조 파악.

questions.passage: His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve.
questions.stem:
위 글의 요지로 보아 빈칸에 가장 적절한 것은?

Matthew Syed's story teaches us that success comes not from natural talent alone, but from __________.
ch: avoiding tasks that seem too difficult
being born with special athletic ability
having a growth mindset and embracing challenges

det.korean: Matthew Syed의 이야기는 성공이 타고난 재능이 아니라 성장 마인드셋과 도전을 받아들이는 태도에서 온다고 가르친다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ growth mindset and embracing challenges: 원문 핵심 — 'had a growth mindset', 'embrace the challenge' 직접 인용.
❌ ① avoiding difficult tasks: 회피형 소년의 태도. 반대.
❌ ② natural ability: 원문은 'ordinary boy'. 타고난 재능 부정.
❌ ③ parental support: 부모 역할은 부차적.
det.tip: growth mindset(성장형 사고방식): 노력으로 능력을 키울 수 있다는 믿음. Carol Dweck 이론.

questions.passage: Think of an ordinary boy who likes playing sports like you and your friends. One day, as he returns from school, his mom and dad are waiting outside and pointing at the garage. His mom smiles and says, "We have a surprise for you." When his dad pulls the garage door open, there is a table-tennis table inside! The boy is excited. He recently joined the school's table-tennis club and wanted to practice more.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: 원문: 'He recently joined the school's table-tennis club.' 소년은 최근 학교 탁구부에 가입했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 학교 탁구부에 최근 가입: 원문 직접 일치.
❌ ① 직접 구입: 부모님의 깜짝 선물.
❌ ③ 학교에서 기다림: 집 밖(outside)에서 기다림.
❌ ④ 관심 없음: excited, wanted to practice more.
det.tip: 내용일치 문제는 원문의 세부 사실을 정확히 확인. recently joined = 최근 가입.

questions.passage: When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room. His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 소년은 공에 팔꿈치를 맞아 멍이 들었다.
다음 주에 아버지가 다시 경기를 제안했다.
소년은 엄마의 제안을 받아들여 형과 경기했다.

det.korean: 원문: 'he turns down her suggestion' — 소년은 엄마의 제안을 거절했다. 받아들인 것이 아님.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 제안을 받아들여 형과 경기: 원문은 turns down(거절). 불일치.
❌ ① 팔꿈치 멍: hitting and bruising his elbow. 일치.
❌ ② 방으로 감: sets the paddle, leaves for his room. 일치.
❌ ③ 다음 주 제안: His dad asks for another game the next week. 일치.
det.tip: turn down = 거절하다. 불일치 문제에서는 반대 의미로 바꾼 선지에 주의.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals. He finds himself at match point, and the audience holds its breath. He serves for the match and sneaks the ball past his opponent. He punches the air in triumph.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 소년은 결승전에서 매치 포인트를 잡고 승리했다.

det.korean: 원문: 'finds himself at match point', 'sneaks the ball past his opponent', 'punches the air in triumph.' 결승에서 승리.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 결승전 매치포인트 승리: makes it to the finals + match point + triumph. 일치.
❌ ① 주말 미연습: on weekends 연습함. 불일치.
❌ ② 준결승 탈락: makes it all the way to the finals. 불일치.
❌ ④ 지역 팀 미가입: is able to join the regional team. 불일치.
det.tip: make it all the way to the finals = 결승까지 진출하다. punch the air in triumph = 승리의 주먹질.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. How about you? Do you see yourself in the story? You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 성장형 사고방식으로 도전을 받아들이는 것의 중요성
탁구를 잘 치기 위한 구체적인 훈련 방법
부모가 자녀의 스포츠 활동을 지원하는 방법
프로 선수가 되기 위해 필요한 타고난 재능

det.korean: 글 전체의 핵심: 성장형 사고방식(growth mindset)으로 도전을 받아들이면 누구나 성장할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 성장형 사고방식 + 도전: growth mindset, embrace the challenge, never give up — 글의 핵심 메시지.
❌ ② 훈련 방법: 구체적 기술 설명 없음.
❌ ③ 부모 지원: 부모 역할은 부차적.
❌ ④ 타고난 재능: ordinary boy — 재능보다 노력 강조.
det.tip: 주제 문제: 글의 반복 키워드(growth mindset, challenge, embrace) 파악.

questions.passage: Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path. His tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task.
questions.stem: 위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: Why Natural Talent Matters Most in Sports
Growth Mindset: The Key to Unlocking Your Potential
How to Become a Professional Table Tennis Player
The Importance of Family Support in Childhood

det.korean: 성장형 사고방식: 잠재력을 여는 열쇠. 글 전체가 growth mindset의 힘을 보여주는 구조.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Growth Mindset: 글의 핵심 개념을 정확히 포착.
❌ ① Natural Talent: 원문은 ordinary boy — 재능보다 노력.
❌ ③ Professional Player: 프로 선수 방법론이 아닌 마인드셋 이야기.
❌ ④ Family Support: 가족 지원은 소재일 뿐 주제 아님.
det.tip: 제목 = 주제를 함축적으로 표현. growth mindset이 글의 중심 키워드.

questions.passage: His dad asks for another game the next week, but the boy still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough. "No, thanks," sighs the boy. <u>"He's going to be better than me anyway."</u> In his eyes, challenges are nothing more than obstacles, and he holds onto the belief that they are best avoided.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 "He's going to be better than me anyway"가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 형이 자신보다 더 많이 연습할 것이라는 확신
형에게 탁구를 가르쳐 달라는 간접적 부탁
도전해도 이길 수 없다는 패배주의적 태도

det.korean: "어차피 형이 나보다 잘할 거야" = 도전해 봤자 이길 수 없다는 패배주의적 태도. 고정형 사고방식의 전형.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 패배주의적 태도: 'anyway'가 핵심 — 시도해 봤자 소용없다는 포기. challenges = obstacles 맥락.
❌ ① 형의 연습량 확신: 연습이 아니라 결과에 대한 체념.
❌ ② 간접적 부탁: 거절(No, thanks) 맥락.
❌ ④ 응원 의지: sighs — 한숨, 긍정적 태도 아님.
det.tip: anyway = 어차피. 고정형 사고방식(fixed mindset): 노력해도 변하지 않는다는 믿음.

questions.passage: When the boy serves the ball, it returns with full force, hitting and bruising his elbow. The boy is not having much fun. He sets the paddle on the table, saying, "I have had enough," and leaves for his room. His dad asks for another game the next week, but <u>he</u> still has some pain in his elbow and just does not feel like taking up the challenge. When his mom suggests playing against his older brother, he turns down her suggestion because his brother is very tough.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 he가 가리키는 사람으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 he = 소년(the boy). 팔꿈치 통증이 있고 도전을 하고 싶지 않은 사람은 소년.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 소년: 앞 문장에서 팔꿈치를 다친 사람이 the boy. he = the boy.
❌ ② 아버지: 아버지는 경기를 제안하는 사람(asks for another game).
❌ ③ 형: 이 시점에서 아직 등장하지 않음.
❌ ④ Matthew Syed: 마지막 문단에서 등장.
det.tip: 대명사 he의 지칭: 문맥상 팔꿈치 통증(pain in his elbow)이 있는 사람 = the boy.

questions.passage: You may have the idea that this is simply a fictional tale. However, this is the true story of Matthew Syed, a former member of the British national table-tennis team. <u>His</u> tale shows how an ordinary boy developed his passion for table tennis and eventually became the national champion. Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new, discovered what he truly desired, and then became tough when he faced a difficult task. You, too, can find your own "table tennis."
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 His가 가리키는 사람으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 밑줄 친 His = Matthew Syed. 바로 앞 문장에서 'the true story of Matthew Syed'라고 밝혔으므로 His tale = Matthew Syed의 이야기.
det.analysis:
✅ ② Matthew Syed: 직전 문장에 Matthew Syed 언급. His tale = Matthew Syed의 이야기.
❌ ① 아버지: 이 문단에서 아버지 언급 없음.
❌ ③ 형: 이 문단에서 형 언급 없음.
❌ ④ 독자: 독자는 you로 지칭.
det.tip: 소유격 His의 지칭: 직전 문장의 고유명사 Matthew Syed를 받는다.

questions.passage: Let's pause the story here. The boy now faces a big choice. He could choose to challenge himself to grow and face difficulties with endurance and courage. Or he could avoid new and challenging experiences and choose an easy, familiar path.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

"소년은 어려움을 인내와 __________으로 맞서는 것과 쉬운 길을 택하는 것 사이에서 선택해야 했다."

(한 단어)

det.korean: 원문: 'face difficulties with endurance and courage' — 인내와 용기.
det.analysis: ✅ courage: 원문에서 직접 찾기. endurance and courage.
det.tip: courage(용기). endurance(인내)와 함께 도전적 태도를 나타내는 핵심 단어.

questions.passage: The boy learns from his mistakes and develops new skills by practicing. He practices hard after school, on weekends, and on holidays until he is able to join the regional team. Eventually, he participates in the national championship and makes it all the way to the finals.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

He developed new skills through constant __________ (practice).

(한 단어)

det.korean: constant + __________ → 형용사 뒤 명사. practice는 동사이자 명사이므로 practice 그대로.
det.analysis: ✅ practice: constant(형용사) 뒤 명사 자리. practice는 동사/명사 동형. through constant practice = 꾸준한 연습을 통해.
det.tip: practice: 동사(연습하다)/명사(연습) 동형. constant practice = 꾸준한 연습.

questions.passage: You, too, can find your own "table tennis." It might be a hobby, a career, or a personal goal. __________ on what you want to achieve. Go out there and achieve your goal!
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 들어갈 문장을 완성하시오. (대소문자 구분 없음, 마침표 생략 가능)

[ what / is / important / is / that / you / embrace / the challenge / and / never / give up ]
questions.wa: What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
accept: What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
what is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up
What is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up.
what is important is that you embrace the challenge and never give up.

det.korean: 중요한 것은 여러분이 도전을 받아들이고 절대 포기하지 않는 것이다.
det.analysis: ✅ What is important(관계대명사절 주어) + is(동사) + that you embrace ... and never give up(보어절).
det.tip: What is important is that ~: 중요한 것은 ~이다. What(관계대명사) + is(동사) + that절(보어).

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"연습이 완벽을 만든다."

→ Practice makes __________.

(한 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'Practice makes perfect.' — 연습이 완벽을 만든다.
det.analysis: ✅ perfect: 속담 'Practice makes perfect.' 원문에서 아버지의 대사로 직접 등장.
det.tip: Practice makes perfect = 연습이 완벽을 만든다. 영어 속담.

questions.stem:
다음 한국어를 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.

"그는 성장형 사고방식을 가지고 있었기 때문에, 새로운 것을 시도했다."

→ Because he had a __________, he tried something new.

(두 단어를 쓰시오)

det.korean: 원문: 'Because he had a growth mindset, he tried something new.' — 성장형 사고방식.
det.analysis: ✅ growth mindset: 원문 직접 인용. growth mindset = 성장형 사고방식.
det.tip: growth mindset(성장형 사고방식) ↔ fixed mindset(고정형 사고방식). Carol Dweck의 이론.
